heading: 1. Metal-Important Genes Are Enriched in the Core Genome

text: Across 22 organisms and 14 metals, metal-important genes are 87.4% core versus a 76.9% baseline (OR=2.08, p=4.3e-162), contrary to the initial accessory-enrichment hypothesis.
quote: Across 22 organisms and 14 metals, genes with significant fitness defects under metal stress are **87.4% core** vs 76.9% baseline (OR=2.08, p=4.3e-162). This is the opposite of the initial hypothesis (H1a), which predicted accessory enrichment for toxic metal genes based on the prior DvH finding (71.2% core for condition-specific heavy-metal genes). The discrepancy arises because genome-wide metal fitness defects predominantly reflect core cellular processes vulnerable to metal disruption (cell envelope, DNA repair, central metabolism), not specialized metal resistance mechanisms.
heading: 1. Metal-Important Genes Are Enriched in the Core Genome

text: Z-scored activity identifies 600 responsive records (|z| > 2.0) among 19,453 module × metal-experiment records (3.1%). DvH has 47 responsive modules across 12 metals; 183 modules with conservation data have mean core fraction 0.826 and median 0.929.

The 183 metal-responsive modules with conservation data have a mean core fraction of **0.826** — consistent with the overall finding that metal fitness genes are core-enriched. heading: 7. Pangenome-Scale Prediction Validates Metal Gene Signature

text: A signature of 1,286 KEGG KO terms scores 27,702 pangenome species. After genome-size normalization, Leptospirillum ranks at the 91st percentile, Acidithiobacillus 77th, Marinobacter 75th, and Sulfobacillus 71st.
quote: A metal functional signature of 1,286 KEGG KO terms was derived from the conserved metal gene families and used to score all **27,702 pangenome species**. With genome-size normalization (metal clusters / total KEGG-annotated clusters), the true specialist bioleaching organisms emerge: *Leptospirillum* ranks at the 91st percentile, *Acidithiobacillus* at the 77th, *Marinobacter* at the 75th, and *Sulfobacillus* at the 71st. However, bioleaching genera as a group are not significantly enriched over background after normalization (Mann-Whitney p=0.17), indicating that metal tolerance genes are broadly distributed across bacteria rather than concentrated in specialists — consistent with the core genome robustness model. Without normalization, species with large open pangenomes (*K. pneumoniae*, *P. aeruginosa*) dominate, reflecting genome size rather than metal biology.

text: The Fitness Browser has no rare-earth-element (REE) experiments.
quote: No REE experiments exist in the Fitness Browser. REEs are the most strategically important critical minerals, and bioleaching/biorecovery of REEs is a rapidly growing field.
heading: Priority 2: Rare Earth Elements (Zero Coverage)

text: Lanthanum chloride at 0.1-1 mM is a proposed, not completed, RB-TnSeq experiment in Putida, Cup4G11, Keio, and Marino.
quote: | **Lanthanum chloride** (0.1-1 mM) | Putida, Cup4G11, Keio, Marino | *Pseudomonas putida* and *Gluconobacter* are studied for REE biosorption. RB-TnSeq under La stress would identify the first genome-wide gene set for REE tolerance. |
heading: Priority 2: Rare Earth Elements (Zero Coverage)

text: Cerium chloride at 0.1-1 mM is proposed for the same organism panel as lanthanum, to compare shared versus element-specific REE tolerance.
quote: | **Cerium chloride** (0.1-1 mM) | Same panel | Ce is the most abundant REE. Comparing La and Ce fitness profiles would reveal whether REE tolerance uses a shared or element-specific gene set. |
heading: Priority 2: Rare Earth Elements (Zero Coverage)

text: Two organisms each have 54 novel metal candidate genes but have been tested against only 1 metal, iron; broader-metal predictions remain unvalidated.
quote: Two organisms have disproportionately many novel metal candidate genes (54 each) but have only been tested against 1 metal (iron). Testing them against the standard metal panel would validate or refute these predictions.
heading: Priority 3: Organisms with High Novel Gene Density

text: Methanococcus maripaludis S2 has 54 novel candidate ortholog groups and metal-fitness testing only for iron; Ni, Co, Cu, Zn, W, and Mo are proposed tests.
quote: | **Methanococcus maripaludis S2** | 54 | Iron only | Ni, Co, Cu, Zn, W, Mo — archaea are underrepresented in metal tolerance studies. These are methanogenic archaea with unique metal cofactor requirements (Ni for hydrogenase, W/Mo for formylmethanofuran dehydrogenase). |
heading: Priority 3: Organisms with High Novel Gene Density

text: Methanococcus maripaludis JJ has 54 novel candidate ortholog groups and metal-fitness testing only for iron; comparison with S2 across a broader metal panel is proposed.
quote: | **Methanococcus maripaludis JJ** | 54 | Iron only | Same panel — cross-strain comparison with S2 would reveal strain-specific metal adaptation. |
heading: Priority 3: Organisms with High Novel Gene Density

text: Pseudomonas putida KT2440 has Fitness Browser fitness matrices but zero metal experiments; the report calls it the only Fitness Browser organism without metal data.
quote: *Pseudomonas putida* KT2440 (Putida) has fitness matrices in the FB but **zero metal experiments** despite being a workhorse for bioremediation and metabolic engineering. It is the only FB organism with no metal data.
heading: Priority 4: The Missing Model Organism

text: Putida has the 5th-highest predicted metal gene repertoire score among Fitness Browser organisms (0.707), but the proposed Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Al, Cr, and U panel has not validated that prediction.
quote: | Full metal panel (Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Al, Cr, U) on Putida | Would immediately link the metal fitness atlas to the extensive *P. putida* engineering literature. Putida has the 5th-highest metal gene repertoire score among all FB organisms (0.707) — testing would validate or refute this prediction. |
heading: Priority 4: The Missing Model Organism

text: The atlas scores 27,702 species, but predictions for species without RB-TnSeq libraries cannot be experimentally validated within the current dataset.
quote: The atlas scores 27,702 species but cannot validate predictions for organisms without RB-TnSeq libraries. Creating libraries for key bioleaching species would bridge the gap between the atlas and industrial applications.
heading: Priority 5: Bioleaching Organisms Not in the FB

text: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans is at the 77th percentile after normalization, but the report says no TnSeq data exist for any Acidithiobacillus species; Fe, Cu, Co, Ni, and Zn tests are proposed.
quote: | ***Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans*** | 77th (norm) | The #1 bioleaching organism. No TnSeq data exists for any *Acidithiobacillus* species. RB-TnSeq under Fe, Cu, Co, Ni, Zn would produce the first genome-wide functional map of bioleaching gene requirements. |
heading: Priority 5: Bioleaching Organisms Not in the FB

text: Geobacter sulfurreducens is at the 53rd percentile after normalization; RB-TnSeq under Fe(III), Mn(IV), and U(VI) reduction conditions is proposed, not reported as completed.
quote: | ***Geobacter sulfurreducens*** | 53rd (norm) | Model metal-reducing bacterium. RB-TnSeq under Fe(III), Mn(IV), U(VI) reduction conditions would identify genes required for extracellular electron transfer and metal transformation. |
heading: Priority 5: Bioleaching Organisms Not in the FB

text: Leptospirillum ferrooxidans is at the 91st percentile after normalization; Fe(II)-oxidation and acid-condition RB-TnSeq tests are proposed, not reported as completed.
quote: | ***Leptospirillum ferrooxidans*** | 91st (norm) | The highest-scoring bioleaching genus after normalization. RB-TnSeq under Fe(II) oxidation and acid conditions would reveal why this genus specializes in bioleaching environments. |
heading: Priority 5: Bioleaching Organisms Not in the FB

text: Expansion from 14 to 16+ metals, 24 to 27+ organisms, and 1-2 to 5+ organisms for critical metals is projected impact conditional on proposed experiments, not an observed result; direct validation of 149 novel candidates is likewise prospective.
quote: If these experiments were performed, the atlas would expand from 14 to 16+ metals (adding REEs), from 24 to 27+ organisms with fitness data, and from 1-2 organisms for critical metals to 5+. The cross-species statistical power for manganese, chromium, uranium, and tungsten would increase from suggestive to definitive. The 149 novel gene candidates could be directly validated in organisms where they are predicted to be important.
heading: Expected Impact
